banner.description: Supercomputer started with two screens on every desk at Higgsfield: an LLM on one, Higgsfield on the other. As image and video models became more capable, creators had more prompts, references, assets, and context to manage around every generation. We decided the system should carry more of that complexity itself. This is how Supercomputer was built.

posts.seoDescription: Supercomputer started with a workflow we kept seeing inside Higgsfield: an LLM open on one screen, Higgsfield on the other. As image and video models became more capable, creators were spending more time managing prompts, references, assets, and context just to use them properly. We decided the system should carry that complexity instead. The first version took about six weeks to build. This is how it happened.

banner.title: Inside Higgsfield #1: How We Built Cinema Studio
banner.description: Cinema Studio started with a kangaroo fighting in an octagon, a viral clip made by naming real cameras and lenses in a prompt instead of describing a look in words. Here's how that experiment became a product built by a 140-person film industry team, five versions shipped in a year, with the engine swapped in ten days when a new model hit the market.

posts.seoDescription: Cinema Studio started with a video nobody on the team could recreate. A kangaroo fighting in an octagon passed a million views in days, but recreating the same quality proved much harder than making the original. What looked like a lucky experiment turned into a year-long effort to understand it, rebuild it, and eventually turn it into a product. Read the full story here.
